subject: Computer Networking
title: Terabit Optical Networks
description: A fast breakdown of Terabit Optical Networks for builders.

hook.text: One fiber strand carries 100 terabits per second. We're nowhere near fiber's physical limits.

buildup.text: WDM sends many colors of light through one fiber. Each color carries its own data stream.

discovery.text: Coherent optics encode data in amplitude, phase, and polarization at once. More dimensions, more data.

twist.text: Hollow-core fiber replaces glass with air. Light moves faster, cutting latency 30%. Great for trading.

climax.text: Multi-core fiber packs seven cores into one cable. Seven times the capacity, no new routes.

punchline.text: Fiber has vast untapped capacity. The bottleneck is electronics, not glass.

quiz.question: How does wavelength-division multiplexing increase fiber capacity?
options: By sending multiple colors of light, each carrying separate data, through one fiber
By making the fiber thicker to carry more light
By increasing the speed of light inside the fiber

details.summary: Terabit optical networks use advanced coherent optics, wavelength-division multiplexing, and hollow-core fiber to push backbone capacity beyond 100 terabits per second on a single fiber. These technologies keep ahead of exponential traffic growth driven by video, cloud computing, and AI workloads.
details.whyItMatters: Global internet traffic doubles every few years. Without continuous advances in optical networking, backbone capacity would become a bottleneck constraining the growth of cloud, video, and AI services.
takeaways: Coherent optics encode more data on each wavelength of light
WDM multiplexes hundreds of wavelengths on a single fiber
Hollow-core fiber reduces latency and increases capacity

faq.question: How does wavelength-division multiplexing work?
faq.answer: WDM sends multiple wavelengths of light through a single fiber simultaneously, each carrying independent data. Dense WDM packs 80 to 100 wavelengths per fiber, each carrying 400 Gbps or more. This multiplies a single fiber's capacity to tens of terabits per second.

faq.question: What is hollow-core fiber?
faq.answer: Hollow-core fiber guides light through air inside the fiber instead of through solid glass. Light travels faster in air than glass, reducing latency by about a third. Hollow-core fiber also reduces nonlinear distortions, enabling higher power levels and longer runs without signal degradation.
